# nonNil

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** `null` or `undefined`.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonNil() — Checks whether a value is **not** `null` or `undefined`. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonNil<T>(value: T | null | undefined): value is T;
```

`nonNil(value)` is the same test as `!isNil(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

The absent values, and only those: `0`, `""` and `false` are present values and do not qualify.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type                     | Description         |
| :-------- | :----------------------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T \| null \| undefined` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not `null` or `undefined`; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `T` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonNil(0); // => true
nonNil(""); // => true
nonNil(false); // => true
nonNil(null); // => false
nonNil(undefined); // => false
```
